## Claims
- [source-backed] Source-2 states \(s_\lambda=\det(h_{\lambda_i-i+j})_{i,j=1}^{\ell(\lambda)}\), with \(h_r=s_{(r)}\) for \(r\ge0\) and \(h_r=0\) for \(r<0\). [source-2, lines 1688-1695]
- [source-backed] The available determinant lemma assumes \(i<k\) and a partition \(\mu\) satisfying \(\mu_k>i\ge\mu_{k+1}\), sets \(\ell=\ell(\mu)\), and states
  \[
  s_\mu=\sum_{m=1}^{k}(-1)^{k-m}h_{\mu_m+k-i-m}s_{\mu^{(m)}},
  \]
  where \(1\le m\le k\) and
  \[
  \mu^{(m)}=(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_{m-1},\widehat{\mu_m},
  \mu_{m+1}-1,\ldots,\mu_k-1,i,\mu_{k+1},\ldots,\mu_\ell).
  \]
  [source-2, lines 1697-1719]
- [source-backed] Its bordered matrix is ordered by inserting the row
  \[
  (h_{i-k+1},h_{i-k+2},\ldots,h_{i-k+\ell})
  \]
  between original Jacobi–Trudi rows \(k\) and \(k+1\), then appending column \(\ell+1\), a duplicate of original column \(k-i\). Thus rows are \(1,\ldots,k,\mathrm{new},k+1,\ldots,\ell\), and columns are \(1,\ldots,\ell,\mathrm{duplicate}\). [source-2, lines 1721-1730]
- [source-backed] The appended column is
  \[
  (h_{\mu_1+k-i-1},\ldots,h_{\mu_k-i},1,0,\ldots,0)^T;
  \]
  this uses \(h_0=1\) and \(h_{\mu_m+k-i-m}=0\) for \(m\ge k+1\). The source says its zero determinant, expanded along that duplicate column, yields the displayed identity. [source-2, lines 1731-1742]
